title: The Loves of Al-Hayfa and Yusuf (Español)

full_text:
In the desert lands of the Banu Hilal lived Princess Al-Hayfa, celebrated throughout Arabia not only for her radiant beauty, but for her peerless mastery of poetry, astronomy, and statecraft. Many proud tribal chieftains sought her hand, but she declared:
'I will marry only a man whose mind matches my own in wisdom, whose heart knows justice, and whose sword defends the helpless.'

From the neighboring tribe came Prince Yusuf, a youth famed for his noble character, modesty, and poetic brilliance.
When Yusuf entered the council of Al-Hayfa's tribe, the two engaged in a famous poetic dialogue, matching rhymed verses on philosophy, virtue, and cosmic law. In each exchange, Yusuf answered with such profound depth and graceful courtesy that Al-Hayfa's heart recognized him as her true equal.

However, a jealous rival chieftain from the north, seeking to prevent their alliance, launched a surprise raid with five hundred lances against Yusuf's encampment.

Instead of waiting for rescue, Princess Al-Hayfa donned a suit of silver chain mail, rallied her tribe's horsemen, and rode alongside Yusuf into battle!
Side by side, their lances moving with coordinated precision, they broke the enemy ranks and captured the aggressor chieftain, sparing his life on condition of perpetual peace.

The two tribes united under their joint rule. Al-Hayfa and Yusuf governed as equal partners in wisdom and justice, building libraries and oases across the desert, remembered for centuries as the model of true union where love and intellect shine together.
moral: Intellectual partnership and shared moral principles form the unbreakable foundation of true love. [ES]
